fact: The Congo ministry of social affairs reports the Registre Social Unique headquarters was inaugurated on 10 April 2026 and, in the minister's words, programmes now have a common source of information through it.
The minister says that thanks to the RSU the assistance programmes, universal health insurance, social safety nets and insertion projects, now have a common source of information.
The World Bank implementation report records 947,013 households registered in the social registry at 30 November 2025, against a target of 857,000, marked as already achieved.

Les Dépêches de Brazzaville reports the Registre social unique, in place since 2015 under the safety nets, is used as the central tool for targeting vulnerable people after a crisis, with households categorised by Proxy Means Test.
Les Depeches de Brazzaville reports that the Registre social unique is a national digital database of vulnerable households, being updated by the Talangai pilot that began 15 January 2026.

The joint arrete of 20 August 2024 describes the registre social unique as a centralised web platform that registers households, generates a unique household identification code automatically and extracts potential beneficiary lists for programmes (articles 2, 5).
Article 8 of the arrete says the registre social unique holds data from the civil-status information systems and the unique identification number, among other sources.
